simple.meaning: חָנַק (chânaq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be narrow ; by implication, to throttle , or (reflex.) to choke oneself to death (by a rope).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in 2 Samuel, Nahum, beginning at 2 Samuel 17:23. The surrounding contexts include family, death, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָנַק (H2614) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חָנַק (chânaq) / H2614 is traced through 2 Samuel 17:23, Nahum 2:13 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to be narrow ; by implication, to throttle , or (reflex.) to choke oneself to death (by a rope)
definitions.full: H2614. chanaq [ חָנַק ] verb strangle (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic חֲנַק , ; Arabic ); — Niph`al Imperfect וַיֵּחָנַ֑ק 2Sam 17:23 strangled himself (+ וַיָּ֫מָת ). Pi`el participle מְחַנֵּק Nahum 2:13 strangle , of lion strangling prey, figurative of Ninevitish king (object not expressed).

occurrences.englishText: When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his donkey, arose, and went home, to his city, and set his house in order, and hanged himself; and he died, and was buried in the tomb of his father.

“Behold, I am against you,” says Yahweh of Armies, “and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions; and I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will no longer be heard.”
